arxiv-1910-10408.title: Controlling the Output Length of Neural Machine Translation
arxiv-1910-10408.description: Abstract The recent advances introduced by neural machine translation (NMT) are rapidly expanding the application fields of machine translation, as well as reshaping the quality level to be targeted. In particular, if translations have to fit some given layout, quality should not only be measured in terms of adequacy and fluency, but also length.

arxiv-2102-05068.title: Low-metallicity Young Clusters in the Outer Galaxy. III. Sh 2-127
arxiv-2102-05068.creator: Chikako Yasui, Naoto Kobayashi, Masao Saito, Natsuko Izumi, and Warren Skidmore
arxiv-2102-05068.description: Abstract In deep near-infrared imaging of the low-metallicity ( [ O / H ] = − 0.7 {\rm[O/H]}=-0.7 dex) H II region Sh 2-127 (S127) with Subaru/MOIRCS, we detected two young clusters with 413 members (S127A) in a slightly extended H II region and another with 338 members (S127B) in a compact H II region.

arxiv-2103-02774.title: Non-Asymptotic Guarantees for Reliable Identification of Granger Causality via the LASSO
arxiv-2103-02774.creator: Proloy Das, and Behtash Babadi
arxiv-2103-02774.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Proloy Das, and Behtash Babadi. Granger causality is among the widely used data-driven approaches for causal analysis of time series data with applications in various areas including economics, molecular biology, and neuroscience. Two of the main challenges of this methodology are: 1) over-fitting as a result of limited data duration, and 2) correlated process noise as a confounding factor, both leading to errors in identifying the causal influences. Sparse estimation via the LASSO has successfully addressed these challenges for parameter estimation.

arxiv-2301-01061.title: New trends in the nanophysics of ferroics, relaxors and multiferroics
arxiv-2301-01061.creator: M. D. Glinchuk, L. P. Yurchenko, E. A. Eliseev
arxiv-2301-01061.description: Abstract The review covers the theoretical and experimental results obtained in the recent years by the scientists with the help of comprehensive investigation of nanoferroics and multiferroics. The main attention will be paid to spontaneous flexoeffects and reentrant phase in nanoferroics as well as to a recently discovered giant magnetoelectric effect in multiferroics.

arxiv-2302-11012.title: Likelihood Annealing: Fast Calibrated Uncertainty for Regression
arxiv-2302-11012.creator: Uddeshya Upadhyay Jae Myung Kim, Cordelia Schmid Bernhard Schölkopf Zeynep Akata
arxiv-2302-11012.description: Abstract Recent advances in deep learning have shown that uncertainty estimation is becoming increasingly important in applications such as medical imaging, natural language processing, and autonomous systems. However, accurately quantifying uncertainty remains a challenging problem, especially in regression tasks where the output space is continuous.

arxiv-2308-08632.title: Advancements in Repetitive Action Counting: Joint-Based PoseRAC Model With Improved Performance
arxiv-2308-08632.creator: Haodong Chen, Niloofar Zendehdel, Ming C. Leu, Md Moniruzzaman, Zhaozheng Yin, Solmaz Hajmohammadi
arxiv-2308-08632.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Haodong Chen, Niloofar Zendehdel, Ming C. Leu, Md Moniruzzaman, Zhaozheng Yin, Solmaz Hajmohammadi. Repetitive counting (RepCount) is critical in various applications, such as fitness tracking and rehabilitation. Previous methods have relied on the estimation of red-green-and-blue (RGB) frames and body pose landmarks to identify the number of action repetitions, but these methods suffer from a number of issues, including the inability to stably handle changes in camera viewpoints, over-counting, under-counting, difficulty in distinguishing between sub-actions, inaccuracy in recognizing salient poses, etc.

arxiv-2402-06389.title: Human Aesthetic Preference-Based Large Text-to-Image Model Personalization: Kandinsky Generation as an Example
arxiv-2402-06389.creator: Aven-Le Zhou, Yu-Ao Wang, Wei Wu, Kang Zhang
arxiv-2402-06389.description: Abstract With the advancement of neural generative capabilities, the art community has actively embraced GenAI (generative artificial intelligence) for creating painterly content. Large text-to-image models can quickly generate aesthetically pleasing outcomes. However, the process can be non-deterministic and often involves tedious trial-and-error, as users struggle with formulating effective prompts to achieve their desired results.

arxiv-2409-18385.title: Robo-CSK-Organizer: Commonsense Knowledge to Organize Detected Objects for Multipurpose Robots
arxiv-2409-18385.creator: Rafael Hidalgo, Jesse Parron, Aparna S. Varde, Weitian Wang
arxiv-2409-18385.description: Abstract In the rapidly evolving field of robotics, integration of commonsense knowledge (CSK) in AI systems is becoming highly crucial to enhance the decision-making capabilities of robots, especially in next-generation multipurpose environments. This paper presents Robo-CSK-Organizer, a pioneering system that employs CSK, via a classical knowledge base, to facilitate sophisticated task-based object organization helpful in multipurpose robots.

arxiv-2504-02931.title: Anatomy of Parity-violating Trispectra in Galaxy Surveys
arxiv-2504-02931.creator: Yunjia Bao, Lian-Tao Wang, Zhong-Zhi Xianyu, Yi-Ming Zhong
arxiv-2504-02931.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yunjia Bao, Lian-Tao Wang, Zhong-Zhi Xianyu, Yi-Ming Zhong. Parity-violating interactions are ubiquitous phenomena in particle physics. If they are significant during cosmic inflation, they can leave imprints on primordial perturbations and be observed in correlation functions of galaxy surveys. Importantly, parity-violating signals in the four-point correlation functions (4PCFs) cannot be generated by Einstein gravity in the late universe on large scales, making them unique and powerful probes of high-energy physics during inflation.

arxiv-2505-06202.title: Guerra interpolation for inverse freezing
arxiv-2505-06202.creator: Linda Albanese, Adriano Barra, Emilio N. M. Cirillo
arxiv-2505-06202.description: Abstract In these short notes we adapt and systematically apply Guerra’s interpolation techniques on a class of disordered mean field spin glasses equipped with crystal fields and multi-value spin variables. These models undergo the phenomenon of inverse melting or inverse freezing .

arxiv-2508-00021.title: Alignment Monitoring
arxiv-2508-00021.creator: Thomas A. Henzinger, Konstantin Kueffner, Vasu Singh, I Sun
arxiv-2508-00021.description: Abstract Formal verification provides assurances that a probabilistic system satisfies its specification— conditioned on the system model being aligned with reality. We propose alignment monitoring to watch that this assumption is justified. We consider a probabilistic model well aligned if it accurately predicts the behaviour of an uncertain system in advance.

arxiv-2509-09489.title: Acoustic to Articulatory Speech Inversion for Children with Velopharyngeal Insufficiency Thanks: This work was supported by NSF Grant No. BCS2141413.
arxiv-2509-09489.creator: Saba Tabatabaee 1 , Suzanne Boyce 2 , Liran Oren 3 , Mark Tiede 4 , Carol Espy-Wilson 1
arxiv-2509-09489.description: Abstract Traditional clinical approaches for assessing nasality, such as nasopharyngoscopy and nasometry, involve unpleasant experiences and are problematic for children. Speech Inversion (SI), a noninvasive technique, offers a promising alternative for estimating articulatory movement without the need for physical instrumentation.

arxiv-2509-24141.title: Thurston spine in a Teichmüller curve

arxiv-2509-24141.description: Abstract . To study the Thurston spine 𝒫 g ⊆ 𝒯 g \mathcal{P}_{g}\subseteq\mathcal{T}_{g} , we construct a Teichmüller curve V ⊆ 𝒯 g V\subseteq\mathcal{T}_{g} . pmc-10595779.title: Individual-level exposures and risk of COVID-19: an umbrella review
pmc-10595779.creator: C Savoia, A M Pezzullo, S Farina, M Di Pumpo, D M Tona, M Porcelli, S Boccia
pmc-10595779.description: As of April 2023, over 650 million people have been confirmed to have contracted COVID-19. The risk of transmission of COVID-19 might be influenced by various factors, including immunity from vaccination or previous infection, the use of personal protective equipment (PPE), indoors vs. outdoors environments, the degree of ventilation in indoor environments, and distance from the source of the infection.

pmc-11345214.title: Editorial: Addressing equity issues in traffic injury prevention
pmc-11345214.creator: Jingwen Hu, Jessica Jermakian, Johan Iraeus, Jonathan Rupp
pmc-11345214.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). s injuries have been reported in older adults, people with obesity, and female occupants, as well as in low-income communities, although the causes of these issues may vary widely. Unfortunately, safety equity will likely get worse without action.

pmc-11631500.title: Addressing public health in times of conflict
pmc-11631500.creator: Charlotte Marchandise, Gauden Galea, Ilmo Keskimäki, Floris Barnhoorn
pmc-11631500.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ublic health governance offer vital lessons for the global public health community. As they become part of the EUPHA network, we look forward to collaborating and learning together to address the significant challenges ahead. Ukraine continues to face relentless attacks that severely impact its public health infrastructure and the endager the life, the health and the mental health of its citizens. At the same time, we must acknowledge the grave situation unfolding in Gaza, Lebanon, and Israel.

pmc-11644193.title: Recent Advancements in Fabrication, Separation, and Purification of Hierarchically Porous Polymer Membranes and Their Applications in Next-Generation Electrochemical Energy Storage Devices
pmc-11644193.creator: Xiong Cheng, Joonho Bae
pmc-11644193.description: In recent years, hierarchically porous polymer membranes (HPPMs) have emerged as promising materials for a wide range of applications, including filtration, separation, and energy storage. These membranes are distinguished by their multiscale porous structures, comprising macro-, meso-, and micropores. The multiscale structure enables optimizing the fluid dynamics and maximizing the surface areas, thereby improving the membrane performance.

pmc-12472265.title: Impact of Four-Phonon Scattering on Thermal Transport and Thermoelectric Performance of Penta-XP2 (X = Pd, Pt) Monolayers
pmc-12472265.creator: Yangshun Lan, Yueyu Zhang, Honggang Zhang, Ping Wang, Ning Wang, Yangjun Yan, Xiaoting Zha, Changchun Ding, Yuzhi Li, Chuanfu Li, Yunjun Gu, Qifeng Chen
pmc-12472265.description: Accurately understanding and modulating thermal and thermoelectric transport in penta-XP2 (X = Pd, Pt) monolayers is crucial for their applications in nanoelectronics and energy conversion. We systematically investigate the thermal conductivity and thermoelectric properties of penta-XP2 monolayers through first-principles calculations, incorporating four-phonon (4ph) scattering and electron–phonon interaction (EPI) effects.

pmc-12523505.title: Impact of Chromium Picolinate on Breast Muscle Metabolomics and Glucose and Lipid Metabolism-Related Genes in Broilers Under Heat Stress
pmc-12523505.creator: Guangju Wang, Xiumei Li, Miao Yu, Zhenwu Huang, Jinghai Feng, Minhong Zhang
pmc-12523505.description: Simple SummaryThis study examined the role of dietary chromium in broiler chickens under heat stress, with special attention to breast muscle metabolism. Chromium supplementation improved growth and reduced fat while lowering stress hormones and improving blood sugar balance. Metabolomic analysis of breast muscle showed that chromium changed key energy and amino acid metabolites, indicating better energy use and fat transport.

pmc-12569781.title: Muscle loss phenotype predicts poor postoperative outcomes of colorectal cancer in US inpatients: a population-based analysis
pmc-12569781.creator: Ko-Chao Lee, Sin-Ei Juang, Kuen-Lin Wu, Kung-Chuan Cheng, Ling-Chiao Song, Chien-En Tang, Hong-Hwa Chen, Kuan-Chih Chung
pmc-12569781.description: PurposeMuscle loss may lead to reduced therapy tolerance and survival. We aimed to assess whether colorectal cancer (CRC) patients with a muscle loss phenotype experience worse outcomes.MethodsData were extracted from the US Nationwide Inpatient Sample for hospitalized patients aged ≥20 years who underwent surgical resection for colorectal cancer (CRC) between 2005 and 2018.

pmc-12609944.title: Perceptual Discrepancies of Opioid Analgesics and Psychotropic Drugs: A Cross-Sectional Study of Korean Patients and Physicians
pmc-12609944.creator: Yongsoo Lee, Eun Hee Chun, Yang-Ki Minn, So Hyun Ahn, Jae Hun Kim, Hee Yong Kang, Hye Sun Lee, Jung Eun Kim, Richard Mario Pino
pmc-12609944.description: Background: Opioid analgesics and psychotropic drugs (medical narcotics) are essential for treating pain and psychiatric disorders. Unlike tiered classification systems used globally, Korea uniformly classifies these medications with illicit drugs under a single narcotics category. This creates misunderstandings among patients and physicians.

pmc-12623517.title: Trends in the Management of Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus by Japanese Practitioners
pmc-12623517.creator: Keiko Arai, Tetsuo Nishikawa, Shohei Yuasa, Koichi Hirao, Hisao Mori
pmc-12623517.description: IntroductionIn recent years, diabetes management by diabetes specialists has evolved owing to various factors such as the introduction of new glucose-lowering drugs. In Japan, many patients with diabetes mellitus are managed by general practitioners (GPs), with the quality of management provided by these GPs playing a crucial role in preventing diabetes-related complications.

pmc-12657657.title: Combining search filters for randomized controlled trials with the Cochrane RCT Classifier in Covidence: a methodological validation study
pmc-12657657.creator: Klas Moberg, Carl Gornitzki
pmc-12657657.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Our objective was to evaluate the recall and number needed to read (NNR) for the Cochrane RCT Classifier compared to and in combination with established search filters developed for Ovid MEDLINE and Embase.com. A gold standard set of 1,103 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) was created to calculate recall for the Cochrane RCT Classifier in Covidence, the Cochrane sensitivity-maximizing RCT filter in Ovid MEDLINE and the Cochrane Embase RCT filter for Embase.com.

pmc-12678504.title: Expert consensus on disease-based long-term follow-up care plans for childhood cancer survivors
pmc-12678504.creator: Jiao-Yang Cai, Ching-Hon Pui, Xiu-Li Ju, Winnie Tso, Ya-Li Han, Wen-Ting Hu, Anthony Liu, Melissa M Hudson, Yin Ting Cheung, China National Children’s Medical Center-Shanghai Long-Term Follow-Up (NCMCs-LTFU) Study Group
pmc-12678504.description: BackgroundChildhood cancer survivors (CCSs) are at increased risk of long-term treatment-related complications. Although international guidelines support risk-based long-term follow-up (LTFU) care, its standardized implementation in China has been limited. To address this gap, the National Children’s Medical Center–Shanghai convened a multidisciplinary expert panel to develop disease-based LTFU care plans tailored to the Chinese healthcare context.

pmc-13091748.title: SIRT3-mediated mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation protects against hepatic lipid deposition in fatty liver hemorrhagic syndrome
pmc-13091748.creator: Panpan Cao, Jinyan Chen, Chun Zeng, Yang Hu, Jianyun Yuan, Xiaoquan Guo, Huabin Cao, Caiying Zhang, Yu Zhuang, Guoliang Hu
pmc-13091748.description: Fatty liver hemorrhagic syndrome (FLHS) is a nutrition-related metabolic disorder in laying hens characterized by excessive hepatic lipid accumulation and hemorrhagic lesions, leading to reduced productivity and increased mortality. However, the regulatory mechanisms linking mitochondrial dysfunction to hepatic lipid metabolism remain unclear. This study investigated the role of SIRT3 in modulating mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation during FLHS progression.

pmc-13264373.title: Perceptions surrounding intranasal naloxone use and access among a population experiencing homelessness
pmc-13264373.creator: Julena Maurer, Sharon Connor, Martha Ndung'u, Brittany Solosky, Judith Okwamba, Linh Huynh, Jessica Abbott, Ian Foo, Anna Marie White, Anita Leon-Jhong, Max Hurwitz
pmc-13264373.description: BackgroundDrug overdose is the leading cause of unintentional death in the United States. Studies suggest people experiencing homelessness (PEH) are at higher risk of overdose. Naloxone, trademarked Narcan®, is a medication that can reverse the effects of an opioid overdose. Despite steps taken to increase the availability of naloxone, opioid overdose deaths continue to occur at alarming rates.

pmc-13359855.title: Benign and Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumors of the Oral Cavity: Two-Case Series Emphasizing Diagnostic Challenges
pmc-13359855.creator: Evgeniy Aleksiev, Dimitar Kosturkov, Tihomir Dikov, Vesela Ivanova, Zornitsa Mihaylova
pmc-13359855.description: Background: Peripheral nerve sheath tumors of the oral cavity are rare and encompass both benign and malignant entities. Differentiating between these lesions remains challenging due to overlapping clinical and histopathological characteristics. Case presentation: We present two cases illustrating the biological spectrum of peripheral nerve sheath tumors in the oral cavity.

pmc-13396238.title: Human angiotensin‑converting enzyme 2‑specific benzothiazole-based allosteric inhibitor against pan‑sarbecoviruses
pmc-13396238.creator: Li Liu, Jinxin Bai, Runhong Zhou, Yao Ma, Dongyan Zhou, Terrence Tsz-Tai Yuen, Wenwu Liu, Pok Man Lai, Wenjun Yu, Jianxin Duan, Jingjia Ye, Xinhua Liu, Ruomei Gong, Ka-Yi Kwan, Tsz Tung Lee, Feifei Liu, Zhenglong Du, Pui Wang, Mengxiao Luo, Dawei Yang, Kong Hung Sze, Hin Chu, Zhiwei Chen, Gang Liu
pmc-13396238.description: Emerging SARS‑CoV‑2 variants and related zoonotic sarbecoviruses rely on ACE2 for cell entry, motivating host‑directed antivirals that block spike-ACE2 interaction. Here, we characterize MB‑32, a benzothiazole small molecule that binds ACE2, selectively disrupts binding of SARS‑CoV‑2 spike receptor‑binding domain to ACE2, and preserves ACE2 enzymatic activity across species.

pmc-13438194.title: End‐to‐end deep learning pipeline for automated IMRT planning in lymphoma: Feasibility and limitations
pmc-13438194.creator: Denis Kutnár, Ivan Richter Vogelius, Hristo Atanasov Georgiev, Katrin Elisabet Håkansson, Lena Specht, Jens Petersen

pmc-13541225.title: Repeat At-Home Saliva Collection to Measure Cortisol Awakening Response (CAR): Protocol Feasibility Study Among Black Women With Histories of Abuse
pmc-13541225.creator: Kiyomi Tsuyuki, Marguerite B Lucea, Andrea N Cimino, Michael Killian, Christina J Catabay, Engle Abrams, Emmanuel Baffour-Siaw, Jacquelyn C Campbell, Douglas A Granger, Jamila K Stockman
pmc-13541225.description: BackgroundEmerging evidence supports that women with histories of abuse have heightened stress and immune dysregulation. Few studies have examined the biological plausibility of this association in US Black women—a population disproportionately affected by gender-based violence (GBV), health disparities, and generally underrepresented in research.

uslaw-usc-t25-s1834.title: 25 U.S.C. § 1834 — Compliance with matching requirement
uslaw-usc-t25-s1834.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t25-s1834.description: United States Code, Title 25 (Indians); Chapter 20 (Tribally Controlled Colleges And Universities Assistance); Subchapter II (Tribally Controlled College Or University Endowment Program). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. For the purpose of complying with the contribution requirement of section 1832(b)(2)(B) of this title, a tribally controlled college or university may use funds which are available from any private or tribal source. Any.
